plan.summary: Add SQLite-backed memory with safe migration and opt-in rollout while preserving JSONL access for one release.

steps.action: Implement SqliteMemory in mirofish_lab/memory.py with local-only sqlite3 persistence, explicit write errors, and a single inspectable table.
steps.rollback: Remove SqliteMemory code and restore the prior JSONL-only memory path.
steps.observability: Table creation succeeds in .mirofish_memory/memory.db; writes raise on failure; no silent drops.

steps.action: Keep LocalMemory signature unchanged and make it a compatibility shim that reads existing JSONL files while writing new entries through the SQLite path.
steps.gate: wait_for:shim tests covering existing JSONL reads
steps.observability: Existing JSONL records remain readable through LocalMemory; new writes land in SQLite.

steps.action: Add migrate_jsonl_to_sqlite() to import all .mirofish_memory JSONL files into SQLite in small batches with loud error handling.
steps.gate: wait_for:successful migration dry-run with record counts matching
steps.rollback: Delete imported rows from memory.db and rerun migration with smaller batch size.
steps.observability: Record counts match on dry-run; disk IOPS and replication lag stay within budget; write failures surface immediately.

steps.action: Add Agent backend selection via backend="jsonl"|"sqlite" kwarg and MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND env var, keeping jsonl as the default.
steps.rollback: Unset MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND and revert Agent default to jsonl.
steps.observability: Agent instantiates the requested backend; default behavior remains unchanged for existing callers.

steps.action: Wire all experiment paths to continue using Agent only, with no per-experiment code changes required.
steps.rollback: Redeploy previous experiment integration that uses Agent without backend selection.
steps.observability: pr-review-rehearsal, pre-flight-rehearsal, adversarial-security-sim, and blast-radius-prediction still run through Agent successfully.

steps.action: Run canary migration on a representative repo and verify imported records are queryable from SQLite.
steps.rollback: Delete memory.db and rerun using JSONL backend only.
steps.observability: Canary repo sees prior reviewer comments in SQLite; migration completes without record-count mismatch.

steps.action: Pilot sqlite opt-in for selected users via MIROFISH_MEMORY_BACKEND=sqlite while keeping the global default on jsonl.
steps.rollback: Switch backend env var back to jsonl and redeploy.
steps.observability: Pilot write error rate is 0; concurrent runs no longer corrupt logs; support readiness and escalation handling are in place.

steps.action: Announce the one-release JSONL default holdback and the opt-in sqlite path before any later default change.
steps.rollback: Revert the default-backend announcement and keep jsonl as default.
steps.observability: Notice is published and acknowledged before any future default flip.

steps.action: After one release and a clean 24h pilot period, flip the default backend to sqlite while retaining JSONL read compatibility.
steps.rollback: Keep default on jsonl and disable sqlite opt-in by env var.
steps.observability: Pilot error rate stays below threshold; no active incidents; rollout occurs outside restricted windows.

steps.action: After 24h of no new JSONL reads or writes, remove legacy JSONL files from .mirofish_memory.
steps.rollback: Restore JSONL files from backup and re-enable LocalMemory shim.
steps.observability: No JSONL access occurs during the quiet period; SQLite remains the only active store.

conflicts.issue: Default backend must stay JSONL for one release and requires notice/approval, while SQLite opt-in and later default flip need gating. Resolved by keeping jsonl default in S4, running opt-in only in S7, and deferring default flip to S9 after notice and pilot success.

Schema creation and migration must happen off-peak, but the implementation work itself has no strict time window. Resolved by making only the table-creation/migration execution steps gated by the off-peak window; code implementation can occur earlier.

Migration must preserve audit trail and avoid silent failures while also throttling bulk inserts to protect replication lag and IOPS. Resolved by requiring dry-run validation, small batches, and explicit error propagation before canary and pilot rollout.
